title: Senate Democrat Opposes Opening Millions of Acres of Public Land for AI Data Centers
summary:
A leading member of the U.S. Senate is signaling a legislative confrontation over the government's effort to grant technology firms access to protected federal acreage for infrastructure development. The move to challenge the plan comes as the Democratic party prepares to take control of Congress next year, transforming the proposal into a focal point for political friction between the legislature and the White House.

The Trump administration, led by Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, is considering a plan to open tens of millions of acres of public lands to permit the buildout of artificial intelligence data centers. The initiative has drawn scrutiny from ProPublica, which reported that Burgum and other officials overseeing these lands hold investments in the AI sector that could profit if the land is commercialized.
